1.title: Dig, Dig, Dig!
1.topic: digging a pit in the sandbox at the park and finding a red lid and a bug (play, outdoors, nature)
lines: It is a *red* *lid*! | I *put* it in my *bag*.
sounds: '이'를 짧고 힘 빼서: dig '딕', pit '핏'. 길게 '이-' 하지 않아요.
입을 옆으로 크게 벌리고 '애': bag '백', pat '팻'.
입에 힘을 빼고 짧게 '어': bug '벅', run '런'.
1.expression: Say “Dig, dig, dig!” with a strong, bouncy beat like you are digging, sound curious on “What is in it?”, lift your voice on “Is it a rock?”, act surprised on “No, it is a bug!”, wave on “Bye, bug!” and finish slow and calm as you pat the sand.

2.title: Mia Learns to Whistle
2.topic: a girl practices all week to whistle like her grandpa and finally whistles a song with him (family, perseverance, feelings)
sounds: f, sh, s, p 뒤는 짧은 t: puffed '퍼프트', clapped '클랩트'.
l, g, 모음, n 뒤는 약한 d: begged '베그드', tried '트라이드'.
2.expression: Start cheerful with Grandpa's happy song, sound eager on “Teach me, please!”, let your voice drop and feel disappointed when only air rushes out, groan for real on “It's too hard!”, give Grandpa a calm, kind voice, get excited on “a tiny tweet popped out!” and end warm and proud as they whistle together.

3.title: How a Letter Travels
3.topic: the journey of a mailed letter from envelope and stamp to mailbox, post office sorting machines, truck or plane, and the cousin's door (community, how things work)
lines: She *puts* it in an *envelope* | and *adds* an *address* and a *stamp*.
A *mail* *carrier* *picks* it *up* | and *takes* it to the *post* *office*.
The *machines* *read* the *address* | and *send* each letter | the *right* *way*.
*Then* the letter *rides* on a *truck* | or *even* an *airplane*! ↘
sounds: machines만 뒤 음절 'CHINES'에 힘! 나머지는 첫 음절을 크게: 'EN-벨롭', 'MAIL-박스'.
'에이'로 끝까지 미끄러지듯: mail '메일', way '웨이'. '멜'처럼 짧게 끊지 않아요.
끝의 -er은 혀를 살짝 말아 약하게 'ㄹ': letter '레러r', carrier '캐리어r'.
3.expression: Read like a friendly tour guide: invite listeners with a rising “Have you ever mailed a letter?”, pause after First, Next, There, Then and At last so each step is clear, sound amazed on “thousands of letters every hour” and “an airplane!”, and ask the last question warmly with your voice going down.
practice: Let's follow one on its trip!

4.title: The Great Kimchi Day
4.topic: a family's November gimjang (kimchi-making day) at Halmeoni's house; a child learns Grandma's leaf-by-leaf trick and that many hands make light work (family, culture, seasons, teamwork)
lines: At *first*, | I *smeared* *paste* on my *apron*, | my *sleeve*, | and *even* my *nose*! ↘
*Everyone* *giggled*, | but *Halmeoni* *showed* me a *trick*: | *start* at the *bottom* | and *work* *up*, | *one* *leaf* at a *time*.
*Halmeoni* *wrapped* *warm* *pork* | in a *fresh* *kimchi* *leaf* | and *popped* it into my *mouth*.
*Now* I *understand* | that *gimjang* isn't *really* about the *kimchi*. | It's about the *hands* that *make* it *together*. ↘
sounds: November는 둘째 'VEM', afternoon은 끝 'NOON'에 힘! cabbage, garlic, ginger는 첫 음절을 크게.
hard g는 목 안쪽 'ㄱ': garlic '갈릭'. soft g는 'ㅈ'에 가까운 /dʒ/: ginger '진저', cabbage '캐비지'.
heads of, jar after jar, popped it into
자음+모음은 이어서: heads of '헤즈어브', jar after jar '자래프터 자', popped it '팝팃'.
4.expression: Tell it like a warm family memory: proud and cozy at the start, shocked on “Fifty?” with your voice going up, worried on “We'll never finish!”, wise and gentle in Halmeoni's voice, list the ingredients smoothly, laugh at the paste on your nose, slow down for Halmeoni's step-by-step trick, sound satisfied as the cabbage disappears, and end thoughtful and slow on the last line.
practice: much too big for my hands
